question: What is the maximum permissible time gap between two sessions of Lok Sabha?
solution:
The correct answer is **__6 months__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The period during which the House of the Parliament meets** to conduct its meeting is called a **session of the Parliament.**
 
• A session lasts from the **beginning of the normal term of house sitting to its end term.**
 
• **The maximum gap between the two sessions should not be more than 6 months. **
 
• This means the **parliament must meet** at **least twice a year. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Current Speaker of Lok Sabha** - Om Birla (June 2019 - present)
 
• **In India, the parliament conducts three sessions each year:**
 
 
• **Budget session**: February to May
 
• **Monsoon session**: July to September
 
• **Winter session**: November to December
